evidence.contextAndScope: End-to-end trust chain from ROM/OTP through TF-A, U-Boot FIT, Linux modules and dm-verity; vendor key hierarchies, anti-rollback, failure logs and key rotation.
evidence.problemSignalAndCounterevidence: The article claimed every platform begins with an eFuse public-key hash and every next stage verifies its successor; generalized TF-A cert semantics and multiple vendor key layouts; supplied unverified Rockchip/TI fuse commands, i.MX IVT/fuse examples and synthetic failure logs. It treated FIT configuration signing as the only policy and module signing/dm-verity as an automatic continuation. Evaluation notes also identify contradictory rollback inequality and a mislabelled AN4581 application note.
evidence.causeHypothesisAndAlternatives: Distinct platform-specific firmware authentication and OS runtime integrity controls were collapsed into one universal chain. Vendor examples were shown without exact platform manuals or executable artifacts.
evidence.evidence: TF-A v2.12.12 TBB documentation defines an optional TF-A authentication implementation; U-Boot v2025.01 FIT docs explain required keys and signed-image/configuration policy; Linux module-signing docs distinguish permissive versus enforced verification. NXP AN4581 is scoped to HABv4/i.MX 50/53/6/7 and is an application note, not a universal reference manual. Sources do not establish unspecified product fuse maps or runtime outcomes.
evidence.sampleCoverage: Read full chapter and published-loop-03 notes, including trust anchor, TF-A cert tree, HAB commands/IVT, Rockchip and TI hierarchies, FIT examples, module signing, anti-rollback, failure messages/logs, summary and links. evidence.decision: Remediated by separating TF-A TBB, FIT verification, module policy and verity boundaries; qualify optional config and enforcement; remove unsupported vendor commands/output and update description to match article scope. URL/date/series/order/draft preserved.
